correctness.rationale: Counting-measure normalization is explicit. A global triangle/convexity inequality bounds the quotient for p>d. Exact norm-equality lattice fibers and an exponential shell estimate control all nonfibers. Endpoint-controlled Riemann sums prove every p<d constant and harmonic summation proves the coefficient 2^d at p=d, with O(1) off-fiber error. The proof is self-contained and finite checker runs only corroborate it.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The smooth Euclidean norm has a thin transverse saddle and a different critical power. Lattice counting and flat-face equality prevent reduction by norm equivalence; the exponential of equivalent norms is not comparable uniformly as |k| grows. General RKHA theorems cover abstract equivalence, not exact family.

value.rationale: The natural cubical norm has full-dimensional flat minimizer fibers, making a distinct exact critical exponent relative to smooth gauges. The theorem determines boundedness and the entire nonbounded power/logarithmic scale with explicit constants in every fixed dimension; it directly informs construction of anisotropic weighted Fourier Hilbert algebras rather than a chosen arbitrary numerical slice.
